prompt: Summarize the excerpt from 'EchoSystems Chrono Compendium v1.0' (chunk 1.3) about time: e term calendar is taken from kalendae,[7][8] the term for the ﬁrst day of the month in the Roman calendar, related to
true_answer: e term calendar is taken from kalendae,[7][8] the term for the ﬁrst day of the month in the Roman calendar, related to the verb calare 'to call out', referring to the 'calling' of the new moon when it was ﬁrst seen.[9] Latin calendarium meant 'account book, register' (as accounts were seled and debts were collected on the calends of each month).[10] e Latin term was adopted in Old French as calendier and from there in Middle English as calender by the 13th century (the spelling calendar is early modern).[10] e course of the Sun and the Moon are the most salient regularly recurring natural events useful for timekeeping, and in pre-modern societies around the world lunation and the year were most commonly used as time units.
